name: Placeholder scRNA-seq
description: SCHEMA EXAMPLE, not a design. Generic single-cell RNA workflow shape, here so the schema, the planner and the twin have something to chew on. Every reagent, time and temperature is a placeholder. The VOLUMES are not arbitrary any more: they are stated as chamber volumes of chip/placeholder_chip_spec.json, because a load fills a chamber and an exchange sweeps one, so a volume that ignores the chamber is not a valid example of anything. Every step says how many chamber volumes it is and why. Loads and single fills are one chamber volume; washes total 4.6 chamber volumes, which is what the 99% exchange goal in contracts/parameters.json needs in a well-mixed chamber, since what is left after V volumes is exp(-V); the release is 3.9, for the 98% release goal. These chambers hold capsules, not adherent cells, so the culture shear ceiling does not apply to them; the bound is capsule.escape_pressure_kpa across the weir, and 50 uL/min puts about 2.5 kPa across a full capsule bed - half the escape pressure, and inside the 0.7 planning margin in contracts/parameters.json. The old 100 uL/min sat exactly ON the escape pressure.

steps.note: Load the capsule suspension into the exchange chamber; the weir holds the capsules back. One chamber volume: a load FILLS the chamber, so the chamber's own volume (3.638 uL) is the only sensible number. This step used to say 100 uL, 27x what the chamber holds.
Wash the capsules three times with wash buffer to clear the loading liquid. SWEEP: 1.5 chamber volumes per wash, 4.6 in total, which is what the 99% exchange goal needs.
Swap in lysis buffer to open the cells, keeping the capsules on the weir. FILL: one chamber volume to put the reagent in; it leaves about a third of the wash buffer behind.
Wash the lysis buffer out three times. SWEEP: 4.6 chamber volumes in total, because carryover into the RT step is what this is for.
Fill the chamber with RT mix. FILL: one chamber volume.
Hold the exchange chamber warm while the RT mix works.
Split the capsules evenly into the four split chambers.
Give split chamber 1 its own reagent, A. FILL: one split-chamber volume (1.273 uL), not one exchange-chamber volume.
Give split chamber 2 reagent B. FILL: one split-chamber volume.
Give split chamber 3 reagent C. FILL: one split-chamber volume.
Give split chamber 4 reagent D. FILL: one split-chamber volume.
Pool the capsules from all four split chambers back into one chamber.
Wash the pooled capsules three times. SWEEP: 1.5 pool-chamber volumes (2.911 uL each) per wash, 4.6 in total.
Release the library from the capsules and send it to the outlet for collection. 3.9 pool-chamber volumes, which is what the 98% release goal needs.
